sources.name: Better Stack on Gartner Peer Insights
Uptime stack pricing discussion on Reddit

claims.statement: Better Uptime launched publicly on May 13, 2020 and later became part of Better Stack.
Better Stack combines outside uptime checks, alerts, on-call schedules, incident work, status pages, logs, traces, metrics, errors, and session replays.
Free includes ten monitors or heartbeats, one status page, Slack and email alerts, and limited logs, traces, metrics, errors, and session replays.
Paid incident response starts at $34 monthly or $29 per responder monthly with annual billing. Other pages, security options, subscribers, checks, ingestion, and retention can add cost.
Quick setup, a clean interface, alerting, integrations, and the useful free plan are common strengths.
Missing features, price jumps, limits, and log-management friction are repeated complaints.

scoreRationale.onboarding: A simple website check and email alert are easy to set up. A real on-call and data setup takes more work.
scoreRationale.product: The joined monitor, incident, status, and data views can speed investigation, but each part must work during a failure.
scoreRationale.support: Support is often praised but was not tested during a live incident.
scoreRationale.billing: Free is generous. Paid cost is difficult to forecast without real responder and data numbers.
scoreRationale.overall: Better Stack is a good place to start monitoring and a plausible tool to combine several operations jobs, provided the team tests a real alert and prices the full stack.

conflictsAndUnknowns: High ratings may not capture rare high-impact failures.
No real outage, alert escalation, log search, or status update was tested.
Data ingestion and retention cost cannot be judged without the team's volume.
